diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive loss on this customer's downstream optical path, most likely a degrading drop fibre, connector, splice, or termination. RX power deteriorated from approximately -22 dBm to below -30 dBm over several days, then readings stopped and the ONU went offline. TX power and laser bias remained stable, so laser degradation is unlikely.
evidence: The ONU is currently offline, has no RX/TX readings, reports MPCP DEREG, and is marked unauthenticated; zero or null optical values indicate no reading rather than a strong signal.

The seven-day RX series shows a sustained progressive decline from about -22 dBm through the degraded range to below the -28 dBm critical threshold, reaching approximately -30.2 dBm before telemetry stopped.
TX power stayed near 2.3 dBm throughout the valid period and TX bias current stayed around 11 mA, both within healthy limits; this argues against ONU laser degradation.
Distance remained constant at 188 m, so there is no evidence of a changed fibre path or distance-change event.
Other ONUs on EPON0/7 are online with normal optical levels, ruling against a PON-port failure or splitter-wide failure.
The OLT is reachable, all eight PONs tested healthy, and CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are normal; this rules against an OLT or OLT-health fault.
VLAN 1057 matches the expected customer VLAN, and RADIUS data is present and CRM-consistent, ruling out provisioning, VLAN, and authentication database faults.
The customer has only two sessions in the last 24 hours and 24 in seven days, so the evidence does not support session flapping or an authentication problem.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service to inspect and clean the ONU, optical outlet, connectors, splices, and customer drop fibre; measure optical loss with a power meter and OTDR; repair or replace the degraded fibre/termination and replace the ONU if its optical receiver is found defective. Recheck ONU registration and RX/TX levels after repair. Do not change the OLT, PON port, VLAN, or RADIUS configuration.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU dropped after four days of progressive optical loss, falling from -22.0 to -31.4 dBm before it stopped registering. The preceding decline indicates a failing fibre path that has now broken, not a power cut.
expected_reasoning: ONU is offline with responds true and online 0, a definite negative
Telemetry shows RX declining from -22.0 to -31.4 dBm over four days before the series ends
The decline crossed the -28 dBm critical threshold roughly a day before the ONU dropped
A progressive decline ending in loss of registration indicates a failing fibre path, not an abrupt power loss
By contrast, a power cut or ONU failure would show a flat healthy signal right up to the cut-off
TX power and bias current were stable throughout, so the laser was not the cause
Peers on EPON0/7 are online with normal readings, bounding the fault to this customer's path
RADIUS is clean, so this is not a suspension
Daily traffic decayed to zero in step with the signal loss
distractors: An ONU reset is the reflex remediation for an offline ONU and will not help here
The telemetry series ends partway through, which could be read as a collection gap
